# UFO Declassified

UFO Declassified is an independent public archive of declassified UAP/UFO records released under the PURSUE initiative (Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters), beginning on May 8, 2026. It indexes all four public tranches released to date: Release 01 (May 8, 2026), Release 02 (May 22, 2026), Release 03 (June 12, 2026), and Release 04 (July 10, 2026).

The archive currently holds **207 document records** spanning **1948–2026**, drawn from U.S. government source groups including the Department of War, FBI, NASA, CIA, Department of Energy, Department of State, ODNI, the Intelligence Community Assessment process, and the National Archives.

The site is designed for research, citation, and source review. Every record links to its official government source, carries source-status labels describing what kind of evidence it is, and includes copy-paste citation text.

- Home: https://ufo-declassified.com/

## Research Tools

Five interactive tools built on the same indexed catalog. These are the pages best suited to citation, data reuse, and answering quantitative questions about the PURSUE releases.

- Evidence Explorer: https://ufo-declassified.com/tools/evidence — Source-status labels across every record. Distinguishes officially unresolved cases from those with a partial explanation on record, official public renditions from raw sensor data, and documents where a specific evidentiary gap has been publicly identified. Each judgment label carries a stated basis.
- Archive Statistics: https://ufo-declassified.com/tools/stats — Full catalog in numbers: breakdown by release, agency, file type, and decade. Includes a CSV download of the complete dataset and a citation block.
- Sighting Map: https://ufo-declassified.com/tools/map — Every locatable record plotted, with honest precision labels (exact site, regional, or approximate). 157 of 207 records carry a location.
- Claim Tracker: https://ufo-declassified.com/tools/claims — Tracks specific UAP claims against what the released records actually support, separating confirmed facts, official statements, and unverified assertions.
- Video Browser: https://ufo-declassified.com/tools/videos — All 85 released UAP video records in one filterable view.
- Release Comparator: https://ufo-declassified.com/tools/compare — What each PURSUE release actually added, resolving the common confusion between cumulative totals and per-release new records.

## Open Dataset

- Full catalog (CSV): https://ufo-declassified.com/dataset/uap-documents.csv
- Permanent archived version (Zenodo, DOI): https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21605258
- Source repository: https://github.com/Starmadebydata/pursue-uap-documents-dataset
- License: CC BY 4.0

The CSV contains one row per indexed record with these fields: `slug`, `title`, `agency`, `year`, `release`, `location`, `file_types`, `evidence_labels`, `record_url`. It is regenerated on every site build.

The catalog is archived on Zenodo with the permanent concept DOI `10.5281/zenodo.21605258`, which always resolves to the latest version. It is released under CC BY 4.0 and is free to reuse, including commercially, with attribution. Preferred citation:

```
Lin, Flynn. (2026). PURSUE UAP Documents Dataset: A structured catalog of declassified
U.S. government UAP records (2026). Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21605258
```

Current composition: Release 01 (31 records), Release 02 (64), Release 03 (72), Release 04 (40). By agency: Department of War (109), FBI (34), NASA (29), CIA (21), Department of Energy (5), Department of State (2), ODNI (1), ICA (1), other (5). By file type: video (85), PDF (74), image (42), audio (7).

## Source-Status Labels

The Evidence Explorer applies two layers of labels. Layer 1 is derived mechanically from record metadata and applies to every record. Layer 2 is editorial and applied only to records this site has researched in depth; each carries a note stating its basis and, where available, a link to the supporting analysis.

Derived labels:
- **Official source linked** — the record carries a link to its official government source page (all 207 records).
- **Public rendition video** — video files are official public renditions, not raw sensor data; chain-of-custody caveats apply (85 records).
- **Historical archival record** — a scanned historical record, valuable as institutional history rather than as a modern case file (66 records).
- **Witness testimony** — the record is primarily first-person account: transcript, debriefing, interview, or case file (54 records).

Editorial labels:
- **Official analysis on record** — an official analytic assessment (AARO, ICA, or agency) exists in the public file.
- **Partial explanation offered** — officials offered a partial or low-confidence conventional explanation, on the record.
- **Officially unresolved** — the releasing agency itself labels the case unresolved or unidentified.
- **Documented context gap** — a specific missing piece (pages, radar data, analysis records) has been publicly documented.

These labels are verifiable statements about a record's sourcing. They are not quality ratings and not judgments about what the underlying event was.

## Citation Guidance

Each document page includes a citation-ready summary, source agency, record year, release date, file package, source/provenance block, canonical URL, and related records.

When citing a record from this site, prefer the document detail page URL and include the named source agency, record year, and PURSUE release date shown on that page.

The Archive Statistics and Sighting Map pages carry a visible "How to Cite" block with copy-paste citation text. Aggregate figures (record counts, per-release breakdowns, agency composition) may be cited from https://ufo-declassified.com/tools/stats.

When citing Culture pages, prefer the native detail page URL and use the visible "How to Cite" block. Culture pages separate fiction, documentary storytelling, journalism, official reports, hearings, and source records so a cultural reference is not confused with primary evidence.

## Source Notes

UFO Declassified is not affiliated with any U.S. government agency. The archive references public domain records released by the U.S. government and provides independent organization, metadata, summaries, source-status labeling, and topic guides.

The site does not assert conclusions about the origin or nature of the phenomena in these records. Where a case is unresolved, it is labeled unresolved. Where officials have offered an explanation, the explanation and its stated confidence level are reported as given.
